title: riverbend-insurance-integration-call-notes-2026-07-02
summary: Initial scoping call with Riverbend Insurance to discuss integrating Redwood Private for policy document summarization and claims triage. Main constraints: on-prem data residency, strict SLA on latency for customer-facing flow, and PHI-sensitive PII handling. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Private but leaning Private because of regulatory requirements.
body:
Call date: 2026-07-02
Duration: 45m
Purpose: scope integration, surface gotchas, next steps and immediate blockers.

Notes: 
- Customer use cases:
  - Real-time policy summarization (user-facing web UI) 
  - Automated claims triage pipeline (batch + occasional interactive review)
  - Embeddings for semantic search across docs (must be stored in their VPC DB)

- Requirements they emphasized:
  - Data cannot leave their network (FedRAMP-ish controls), so Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is preferred.
  - Expect SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for short prompt summarization (<=256 tokens) in web UI.
  - Batch throughput requirement for triage: ~2k docs/day with bursts up to 20k/day monthly.
  - Audit logs and KMS/HSM integration required for key management.
  - Support for redaction of PHI before indexing; want deterministic redaction stage (they may run local preprocessor).

- Auth / networking:
  - They'll provision private peering and mention AWS Direct Connect to our Private control plane.
  - Marcus: Redwood supports VPC peering + customer-managed NAT for egress. Need to confirm allowed ports and CIDR ranges.
  - Priya: wants short checklist for firewall rules and certificate fingerprint steps.

- Model & runtime considerations:
  - They asked about model variants for latency vs quality. We suggested 3-tier approach: low-latency quantized variant for UI, standard FP16 for batch quality jobs, and a high-quality fallback (larger model) for edge-case review.
  - KV cache / prefix caching recommended for web UI to hit latency SLO with repeated prompts. Marcus to propose cache TTL defaults and sizing guidance.

- Privacy & compliance:
  - Must ensure no logs leave their environment. Redwood: Private deploy can optionally disable telemetry and keep audit logs local. Need to document exactly which telemetry is optional.
  - KMS integration: they use AWS KMS with custom key rotation policy. Marcus to confirm Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM with that rotation cadence.

- Gotchas / Risks surfaced:
  - 95th pctl 250ms is aggressive for on-prem depending on hardware. Need to baseline. Recommend dedicated GPUs (A10/A100 equivalent).
  - Embedding storage: they plan to use their existing vector DB inside VPC. Need to verify network latency between model nodes and DB; consider colocating embedding service.
  - Model size vs memory: some of their docs are long (up to 8k tokens); for summarization we recommended chunking strategy + reorder for critical fields.
  - Rollout policy: want canary traffic split by tenant ID. Confirm Redwood rollouts can do per-tenant routing in Private.

- Immediate action items called out on the call:
  - Marcus: produce a one-page install/network checklist (firewall ports, CIDR, cert thumbprints, control-plane endpoints) by 2026-07-06.
  - Jordan: draft commercial outline (Private licensing + support) and expected lead times for dedicated hardware by 2026-07-08.
  - Samira: open JIRA (RWD-7821) to track KMS questions and telemetry opt-out details.
  - Priya: share sample doc set (anonymized) and a redaction spec by 2026-07-09 so we can run a perf spike test.

- Notes for engineering follow-up:
  - Need to run a perf baseline inside a customer-like environment: target config A100x1 (or A10x2) with 32GB RAM per node, pinned to FP16 and quantized variants. Measure 95th latency for 256-token prompts.
  - Evaluate embedding throughput: bulk encode 20k docs and report time + memory.
  - Confirm Private control plane deployment model: air-gapped option + periodic signed manifest updates.

- Communication preferences:
  - Customer prefers Slack for technical threads (they will invite us to #riverbend-integration).
  - Weekly standup during onboarding (first 3 weeks), then biweekly. Jordan to set calendar invite.

- Misc:
  - Priya asked about model explainability logs (token-level scoring). Marcus said we can provide token-level logits in debug mode but must ensure opt-in and local-only retention.
technical_notes: Recommend hardware baseline: 1x A100 (or 2x A10) for initial latency targets; exact sizing to be validated with perf run.
KV/prefix cache: suggest default TTL 10m for UI; sizing depends on active user concurrency (need Priya's concurrency estimate).
Embedding service: run inside the same VPC and ideally same AZ as model nodes to minimize network hops.
Redaction: customer will provide local preprocessor; Redwood to accept already-redacted input or provide a hook for local plugin.
Rollouts: confirm per-tenant routing for Private (A/B/canary based on tenant ID).
Telemetry: document all optional telemetry flags for Private control plane and runtime (audit logs, usage metrics, anon-telemetry).
open_questions: What exact firewall ports and CIDR ranges do we need to document for VPC peering?
Does Redwood Private support the customer's KMS rotation cadence (monthly)?
Can we meet 95th pctl 250ms on recommended hardware without aggressive quantization?
Is per-tenant canary routing already available in the Private product (or needs a small feature dev)?
Can we accept embeddings stored in their vector DB without additional replication?
action_items: Jordan: commercial outline and lead times (due 2026-07-08)
Samira: open JIRA RWD-7821 to track KMS & telemetry questions (done 2026-07-02)
Priya: share anonymized sample docs + redaction spec (due 2026-07-09)
Eng: schedule perf baseline run once sample docs received
next_steps: Send calendar invites for weekly onboarding (Jordan)
Share checklist + network guide with Riverbend (Marcus)
Schedule perf run with eng (Samira to coordinate)
Follow-up email summarizing call + attach list of open questions (Samira)
Create internal design spike doc after perf results (eng)
